# S142 — Slim the README to a front page and give each doc topic one home

The README is about 435 lines and duplicates material that also lives in docs/. The install section is nearly word for word the same as getting-started §1, and the two copies have already drifted. Batch changes and goals/non-goals appear in both. Long `next`/`list`/`--render --strict` notes overlap docs/agents.md. Three separate "see also" paragraphs each link a different set of pages.

**Findings:** docs review: README duplicates install, batch, goals and next/list detail from docs · **Size:** M · **Tree:** slicer

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

Duplicated docs drift, and a long README buries the pitch and quick start. The README should be the front page: what slicer is, how to install it, a first run, a compact command table, and one index of the docs. Each topic should have exactly one full treatment that everything else links to.

## Files

- `README.md`: reduce to the pitch, a short install (the venv block with a link to getting-started for alternatives and editable installs), the quick-start block, a compact command table with one line per command, a single Documentation list, and short Tests/Status sections.
- `docs/commands.md` (new): the human-facing command reference moved out of the README, covering `next` offsets and `--ready`, `list` columns, `--render`/`--strict`, priority scoring, the git allowlist, batch changes, the `.slicer/` layout and merge driver, removing items, roadmap prose, and goals/non-goals.
- `docs/getting-started.md`: sole full install section; link to commands.md where it currently repeats reference detail.
- `docs/agents.md`: link to commands.md rather than restate human-facing detail; keep its JSON contracts.
- `AGENTS.md`: fix any README anchors this breaks.
- `src/slicer/` and tests only if they reference README anchors or sections by name.

## Failing tests

None; documentation only, unless a test or `slicer ai instructions` references a moved README anchor, in which case update it and its test together.

## Implement

Inventory each README section and assign it one home: README, getting-started, commands.md, agents.md, configuration.md, or tui.md. Move content rather than rewriting it, and delete the duplicate once the kept copy is complete. Where the two install copies differ, keep the getting-started wording and carry over anything only the README has. Replace the three README link paragraphs with one Documentation list naming every page in docs/ plus ARCHITECTURE.md, AGENTS.md and CHANGELOG.md. Search the repo (`rg 'README.md#'`) for anchors into moved sections and update them.

## Check

No topic has a full treatment in more than one file. The README is a front page (target: under about 150 lines). Every relative link and anchor in README.md, AGENTS.md and docs/*.md resolves. `rg 'README.md#'` finds no stale anchors. `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer check`, the unittest suite, and `git diff --check` pass.

## Git

Review the documentation, state, and generated markdown together. Leave commit, merge, push, and publication to the owner.
